newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Cocoa past its peak, eyes support.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Cocoa past its peak, eyes support.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures have seen their immediate top and may pull back for September to test the closely watched 1,000 stg a tonne support, traders said on Wednesday.
They called the market to open 10 stg lower.
After slipping to a four-month low of 965 stg on July 24, the London futures came back again to touch an intra-day high of 1,028 on Tuesday morning.
But the upward momentum came to a halt in the afternoon after New York took a downturn.

The U.S. market ended sharply lower and towards the bottom of the day's range on Tuesday, pressured by speculative selling, dealers said. September cocoa fell $29 per tonne on the day, to $1,510, after ranging between $1,538 and $1,508.
Traders said the London market had probably seen its peak.
"Cocoa has worked higher. It may test 1,000 on September," said one trader.
A break below 1,000 could attract strong support at 989, followed by the most recent low of 965.
On the upside, the market faced a cluster of resistances starting from 1,030 and then 1,045.

Players were also closely watching sterling. Weaker sterling against the dollar and mark had helped the cocoa market to recover from last week's falls, which had been aided by the strength of the British currency.
